notes:
Overview: Faraday Works builds edge telemetry & fleet management for industrial vehicles. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated to run low-latency telemetry summarization and an internal support assistant.

Key ask: guaranteed sustained throughput for two models (telemetry-summarizer-v2, support-assistant-3B-qa) with 99th pct latency SLOs and reserved GPU planning for predictable monthly spend. Team wants clear fallbacks + routing to cheaper quantized variants under load bursts.

From AE call (Jordan): 'We need predictable tail latency during morning and evening batch windows; cost controls are critical — procurement will insist on commitment ranges and rollover credits.'

Security notes: Must support SSO via SAML, customer-managed KMS, and 90-day audit log retention. Data residency requirement: NA-only for PII extracted from telemetry.

Gist of POC: 3-week Dedicated POC: week1 deploy + smoke, week2 load/soak at baseline, week3 stress + failover. Representative prompts attached in POC plan.

POC constraints: cannot use hosted API (corporate policy), firewall egress limited to whitelisted Redwood endpoints, on-prem proxy for metrics aggregation (Telemetry team).

use_case_summary: Primary workload: near-real-time telemetry summarization (short sequences, frequent requests) + internal support assistant handling reranking of diagnostic results. Targets: 50k reqs/day, peak 600 qps during fleet rollouts, 99th pct latency < 120ms for summarizer and < 350ms for support-assistant. Cost sensitivity: high — want committed capacity with burst economics and quantized fallbacks.
poc_plan: Scope: Dedicated cluster (VPC) with 8 reserved GPUs equivalent for baseline; capacity can burst to 12 with autoscale policy
Phase A (Week 1) - Deploy models, integration tests, KV cache warmup, smoke latency checks (representative prompts run)
Phase B (Week 2) - Throughput load tests: ramp to 70% baseline sustained for 8 hours, measure p50/p95/p99, token-throughput and CPU/GPU utilization
Phase C (Week 3) - Soak test: 48-hour sustained 50% baseline + 4 simulated morning peaks to validate routing/fallbacks
Failure modes: run simulated GPU preemption and network throttling to validate automatic fallback to quantized variant and cross-region failover
Metrics tracked: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, cost-per-1M-tokens, queueing delay, error-rate, cache hit-rate
Success criteria: p99 latency under SLO during 70% sustained load; failover time < 5s with <1% error spike; predictable cost model within +/-12% of quote
representative_prompts: Telemetry summarization: 'Summarize the last 5 minutes of vehicle telemetry focusing on anomalies, battery, and temperature events.'
Reranking: 'Rank the diagnostic candidate causes for error code E-47 and provide probable root cause with confidence scores.'
Support assistant: 'How do I recalibrate sensor X on firmware 3.2? Provide step-by-step and commands.'
Short-chatlet: 'List top 3 alerts in free text for operator dashboard for vehicle 1287.'
benchmark_results: Early lab sim (SE-run) - baseline simulation suggests 8 A100-equivalent GPUs can sustain 420 qps for summarizer at p95=45ms, p99=95ms. Support assistant heavier (longer seq) showed p95=230ms, p99=380ms under same baseline — slightly above target for p99. Cache warmup increases initial spikes; recommend pre-warming + prefix caching. Quantized variant reduced GPU utilization by ~35% in sim but increased p99 by ~25ms.
negotiation_points: Guaranteed throughput tiers and credits for underutilization
Tail-latency SLA with specific p99 windows and measurement methodology
Reserved GPU sizing + rollover policy for committed months
Penalty clauses vs credits for sustained SLA misses (>3 consecutive hours)
Right-to-audit and security artifact delivery timelines
